newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dostum agreed to join battle against Taleban - paper.
newsitem.headline: Dostum agreed to join battle against Taleban - paper.

text.p: Afghanistan's northern leader Abdul Rashid Dostum has agreed to join the battle with the ousted Afghan government against the fundamentalist Taleban, the London-based al-Hayat newspaper reported on Tuesday.

The Arabic-language paper quoted sources close to Dostum as saying the Uzbek warlord had agreed at a five-hour meeting at the top of the Salang Pass on Monday "to enter the battle (against Taleban) within three days".
Dostum had on Monday recognised the ousted government of Burhanuddin Rabbani but held back from joining a military alliance with its forces around Kabul.
The fundamentalist Taleban, rulers of most of Afghanistan for the past two weeks, admitted losing towns on the road north of Kabul but vowed they would roll Rabbani forces back.

General Dostum, estranged from the Rabbani government and especially from Rabbani's Defence Minister, Ahmad Shah Masood, since 1994, has been much courted since Taleban forces drove the government out of Kabul little more than two weeks ago.

Dostum's recognition of Rabbani as the legitimate head of state during his second meeting with Masood in a week suggests a ring of hostile forces is being set in place around the mainly Pushtun Taleban, who now occupy about two-thirds of Afghanistan.
Dostum controls six provinces north of the Hindu Kush mountains and Afghan watchers say his support is key to any push by Masood and his political mentor Rabbani to recover power.
